TEST FIXTURE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
==============================

This document describes the fixture management system for kafka-scribe integration tests.

OVERVIEW
--------

The fixture management system provides a comprehensive solution for managing test fixtures and test data. It supports:

1. Versioned test data - Test data is versioned using semantic versioning (major.minor.patch)
2. Organized and documented fixtures - Fixtures include metadata and are organized in a directory structure
3. Automated data generation - Different types of test data can be generated for various scenarios
4. Support for different test scenarios - Basic, filtered, error, high volume, and custom scenarios
5. Cleanup utilities - Temporary directories are automatically cleaned up

DIRECTORY STRUCTURE
------------------

When using the FixtureManager, fixture directories will be created with the following structure:

fixtures/
└── <fixture-name>/          # Name of the fixture
    ├── latest/              # Symlink to the latest version
    └── <version>/           # Version directory (e.g., "1.0.0")
        ├── metadata.json    # Fixture metadata
        ├── all_messages.json # Combined file with all messages
        └── messages/        # Directory containing individual message files
            ├── message-00000.json
            ├── message-00001.json
            └── ...

FIXTURE MANAGER FEATURES
-----------------------

1. Creating a Fixture Manager
   - Create with default fixtures directory
   - Create with a specific seed for reproducible data

2. Creating a Fixture
   - Specify version information (major, minor, patch, description)
   - Add tags for categorization
   - Include custom properties
   - Generate test messages for different scenarios

3. Loading a Fixture
   - Load the latest version of a fixture
   - Load a specific version of a fixture
   - Load fixture metadata

4. Listing Fixtures and Versions
   - List all available fixtures
   - List all versions of a fixture

5. Temporary Directories
   - Create temporary directories for tests
   - Automatically clean up temporary directories

SCENARIO TYPES
-------------

The FixtureManager supports different scenario types for generating test data:

1. Basic - Simple messages with standard structure
2. Filtered - Messages with specific key patterns for testing filtering
3. Error - Messages with potential error conditions (invalid UTF-8, large payloads)
4. HighVolume - Large number of messages for performance testing
5. Custom - Messages with custom key patterns

BEST PRACTICES
-------------

1. Version Your Fixtures - Always use semantic versioning for fixtures to track changes
2. Document Your Fixtures - Add descriptive metadata to fixtures to explain their purpose
3. Use Tags - Tag fixtures to categorize them and make them easier to find
4. Clean Up - Always clean up temporary directories after tests
5. Use Specific Seeds - For reproducible tests, use specific seeds when creating fixture managers
6. Choose Appropriate Scenarios - Select the scenario type that best matches your test requirements

IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS
--------------------

The fixture management system is implemented in the tests/common/fixture_manager.rs module. It includes:

1. FixtureVersion - Struct for versioning test data
2. FixtureMetadata - Struct for storing metadata about fixtures
3. ScenarioType - Enum for different test scenarios
4. FixtureManager - Main struct that provides methods for managing fixtures

The FixtureManager integrates with the existing test_data.rs and dir_helpers.rs modules to provide a comprehensive solution for test data management.

For detailed usage examples, refer to the inline documentation in the fixture_manager.rs file.
